name: Venezuela

system.type: Single-round plurality presidential vote; electronic voting with paper tally sheets

wildFacts.text: Opposition poll watchers collected tally sheets (actas) from 80% of precincts; they showed González winning.
The Carter Center said the election did not meet international standards and it could not verify the CNE result.
US forces seized Maduro in January 2026; Delcy Rodríguez became interim president.

notes: The CNE's officially reported figures (2 August 2024) are quoted by the UN Panel of Experts, which notes that no polling-station results were published; turnout was 59.97%. The result is disputed: the opposition's tally sheets showed González winning (Carter Center). An earlier figure in the research came from the CNE's 29 July first bulletin, which was superseded. Maduro's capture is confirmed by Semafor and Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/3/us-urges-venezuela-to-follow-phased-plan-for-democratic-transition). Venezuela abolished compulsory voting, which was practised from 1958 to 1993, per International IDEA (https://www.idea.int/data-tools/data/voter-turnout-database/compulsory-voting). No new election date has been set.
nationalWinner: Nicolás Maduro (officially reported by CNE; disputed)
